subject: event-based embedded eye tracking
claim: An embedded DVS-based eye-tracking system demonstrated sub-millisecond end-to-end latency with low energy per inference, showing that event-based sensing can shift gaze tracking toward sparse asynchronous processing.
mechanism: asynchronous event sensing plus embedded spatiotemporal pupil inference
limitations: Prototype metrics do not establish performance across all eye-tracking conditions or commercial XR constraints.

sources.title: Embedded event-based eye-tracking prototype using DVS and STM32 from FARMAKSIA research cycle

subject: multi-state geometric-phase varifocal optics
claim: Stacked QWP geometric lenses can generate exponentially increasing discrete focal states; a two-layer prototype demonstrated nine focal states over a broad accommodation range.
limitations: Discrete focal-state switching does not reproduce a continuous light field and practical XR integration remains a prototype challenge.

sources.title: QWP geometric-lens multi-state varifocal XR study from FARMAKSIA research cycle

subject: adaptive optics full-field swept-source OCT
claim: Adaptive optics combined with full-field swept-source OCT and structured DMD illumination can increase retinal spatial and temporal observability at cellular scale.
mechanism: adaptive wavefront correction plus structured illumination and high-speed volumetric OCT
limitations: Conference-stage prototype with limited validation relative to mature clinical OCT.

sources.title: Adaptive-optics full-field swept-source OCT prototype from FARMAKSIA research cycle

subject: OLED temporal modulation / stroboscopic visibility
claim: OLED stroboscopic artifacts can remain visible at high PWM frequencies under some low-luminance and duty-cycle conditions; visibility depends on more than nominal refresh/PWM frequency alone.
mechanism: temporal light modulation interacting with visual temporal sensitivity
limitations: The study measured stroboscopic visibility, not long-term fatigue, injury or clinical harm.

sources.title: OLED stroboscopic visibility study from FARMAKSIA research cycle

subject: white-point adaptation and visual comfort
claim: Perceptually neutral white and visually comfortable white need not coincide; adaptation shifted neutrality across the tested CCT range while comfort remained centered near a more stable region.
mechanism: chromatic adaptation and perceptual comfort as distinct objective functions
limitations: Small sample and specific viewing environment; comfort is not a universal physiological optimum.

sources.title: White-point neutrality versus visual-comfort study from FARMAKSIA research cycle

subject: metalens light-field XR display
claim: A 2026 metalens light-field XR prototype demonstrated a wide field of view, millimeter-scale eyebox and accommodation support from near distance to optical infinity.
mechanism: light-field angular sampling through metalens-based optical architecture
limitations: Prototype-scale validation; manufacturability, efficiency and user-level optical quality require broader evaluation.

sources.title: 2026 metalens light-field XR prototype from FARMAKSIA research cycle

subject: super-resolving adaptive-optics OCT
claim: Annular illumination combined with sub-Airy detection improved lateral resolution of in-vivo adaptive-optics OCT beyond the conventional configuration and better separated human photoreceptor mosaics.
mechanism: joint point-spread-function/transfer-function engineering through illumination and detection geometry
limitations: Experimental instrumentation and signal/aperture trade-offs remain; extensive clinical validation is absent.

sources.title: Communications Engineering study: AOOCT beyond the diffraction limit

subject: spatiotemporally controlled illumination for event cameras
claim: Controlling illumination in space and time can prevent event-rate overflow and extend event-camera operation to substantially denser particle fields than conventional illumination.
mechanism: active redistribution of event density within finite sensor/bandwidth capacity
limitations: Demonstrated in particle-image velocimetry, not retinal imaging or human vision; transfer to other event-camera tasks is an inference.

sources.title: Optics Letters study: spatiotemporally controlled illumination for event-based PIV

subject: liquid-crystal microlens event camera for HDR/static scenes
claim: An electrically controlled liquid-crystal microlens array can deliberately vary the PSF so that static scenes generate temporal changes measurable by an event sensor, enabling intensity/event fusion for HDR reconstruction.
mechanism: active computational optics plus event sensing and temporal fusion
limitations: Requires extra optical modulation and learned fusion; the relative contribution of optical coding versus reconstruction network remains to be isolated.

sources.title: Optics Express study on LC-MEC active event camera for static/HDR scenes
